turns.question: Did Anthropic make money in the first half of 2026?
turns.memo: No on a GAAP basis, yes on an adjusted basis for the six months ended June 30, 2026. The filing reports an operating loss of $693m for the six months ended June 30, 2026. It reports a net loss of $80,748m for the six months ended June 30, 2026. It separately reports Adjusted Operating Income of $1,618m for the six months ended June 30, 2026. It separately reports Adjusted Net Income of $2,671m for the six months ended June 30, 2026.

turns.question: Why is GAAP net loss so large?
turns.memo: The filing reports net loss of $80,748m for the six months ended June 30, 2026. The size mainly reflects change in fair value of convertible notes, derivative liabilities, and SAFEs of $72,388m for the six months ended June 30, 2026. It also reflects other income (expense), net expense of $8,757m for the six months ended June 30, 2026. The filing says the fair-value change was primarily driven by an increase in the fair value of outstanding convertible promissory notes from higher enterprise valuation.

turns.question: How does Adjusted Net Income differ from GAAP?
turns.memo: The filing reports net loss of $80,748m for the six months ended June 30, 2026. It reports Adjusted Net Income (Loss) of $2,671m for the six months ended June 30, 2026. The difference adds back stock-based compensation expense of $2,185m for the six months ended June 30, 2026 and non-cash charitable contributions of $126m for the six months ended June 30, 2026. It also adds back change in fair value of convertible notes, derivative liabilities, and SAFEs of $72,388m for the six months ended June 30, 2026 and change in fair value of certain mark-to-market financial instruments of $8,720m for the six months ended June 30, 2026.
